See further details below.

Salary and employee benefits expense increased $3.3 million and $21.4 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 , respectively, as compared to the same periods in 2025. The increase for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was mainly due to increases in cash incentive and stock-based compensation, partially offset by lower severance expense. pretax.text: Income before income taxes generated by the Consumer Banking segment increased $14.1 million to $45.0 million for the third quarter 2026 as compared to the third quarter 2025 mainly due to higher net interest income combined with lower provision for credit losses, partially offset by higher non-interest expense. Net interest income for this segment increased $13.2 million mainly due to additional interest income generated from higher average loan balances coupled with a decline in our funding costs compared to one year ago. The provision for credit losses decreased $3.8 million for the third quarter 2026 as compared to the same quarter in 2025 mainly due to the continued low level of charge-offs within the residential mortgage portfolio. Non-interest expense increased $3.1 million for the third quarter 2026 mostly due to increases in professional and legal fees and other general operating expenses within the other segment items category. See further details in the “Non-Interest Income” and “Non-Interest Expense” sections of this MD&A.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income tax expense totaled $37.3 million for the third quarter 2026 as compared to $49.6 million for the second quarter 2026 and $46.6 million for the third quarter 2025. Our effective tax rate was 15.3 percent, 22.5 percent and 22.2 percent for the third quarter 2026, second quarter 2026 and third quarter 2025, respectively. The decrease in our effective tax rate for the third quarter 2026 as compared to both prior periods was primarily due to the purchase of additional tax credits in excess of amounts previously anticipated during the third quarter 2026.

GAAP requires that any change in judgment or change in measurement of a tax position taken in a prior annual period be recognized as a discrete event in the quarter in which it occurs, rather than being recognized as a change in the effective tax rate for the current year. Our adherence to these tax guidelines may result in volatile effective income tax rates in future quarterly and annual periods. Factors that could impact management’s judgment include changes in income, tax laws and regulations, and tax planning strategies. Based on the current information available, we anticipate that our effective tax rate will be approximately 20 percent for the full year 2026.

capex.text: Valley's short- and long-term cash requirements include contractual obligations under borrowings, deposits, payments related to leases, capital expenditures and other purchase commitments. In the ordinary course of operations, the Bank also enters into various financial obligations, including contractual obligations that may require future cash payments. Management believes the Bank has the ability to generate and obtain adequate amounts of cash to meet its short-term and long-term obligations as they come due by utilizing various cash resources described below.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income on a tax equivalent basis of $506.8 million for the third quarter 2026 increased $18.4 million and $59.3 million compared to the second quarter 2026 and the third quarter 2025, respectively. Interest income on a tax equivalent basis increased $27.8 million to $858.5 million for the third quarter 2026 as compared to the second quarter 2026. The increase was primarily due to higher yields on adjustable interest rate loans, the origination of higher-yielding loans within the commercial and industrial and commercial real estate loan portfolios, an overall increase in average loan balances, and one additional day during the third quarter 2026 as compared to the second quarter 2026. Total interest expense increased $9.4 million to $351.7 million for the third quarter 2026 as compared to the second quarter 2026 mainly due to an increase in average time deposits during the third quarter 2026, as well as the higher cost of certain non-maturity deposits.

Average interest earning assets increased $3.2 billion to $61.8 billion for the third quarter 2026 as compared to the third quarter 2025 largely due to growth in the loan and investment securities portfolios over the last 12-month period, partially offset by lower levels of overnight interest bearing cash balances during the third quarter 2026.

intro.text: As the principal subsidiary of Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ: VLY), Valley National Bank is a regional financial institution with over $66 billion in assets. Founded in 1927, Valley has more than 220 branch locations and commercial offices nationwide and serves clients across New Jersey, New York, Florida, Alabama, California, Illinois, Pennsylvania and Arizona. Valley delivers a full range of consumer, commercial, and wealth management solutions designed to support everything from homeownership and business growth to long-term financial planning. Big enough to support complex financial needs and small enough to stay deeply connected, Valley is grounded in a relationship-led approach focused on understanding people first. That same relationship-led approach guides Valley’s commitment to community investment and responsible corporate citizenship.
